flashcards.q: Which service for DNS-global, L4, regional-L7, global-L7?
flashcards.a: Traffic Manager = DNS-only (TTL-slow failover); Load Balancer = L4 TCP/UDP regional/cross-region; Application Gateway v2 = L7 regional; Front Door = L7 global anycast edge.

flashcards.q: Basic Load Balancer status and Standard differences?
flashcards.a: Retired September 30, 2025 (existing run unsupported, no SLA). Standard: zone-redundant, secure-BY-DEFAULT (needs NSG allow), explicit outbound rules, HTTPS probes, ~99.99% SLA, static Standard IPs only.
Regional L7: path/host routing, WAF OWASP CRS, cookie affinity, autoscaling 0-~125 units; deploy per-workload not shared in hub (CAF guidance).

flashcards.q: What does Front Door add at the edge?
flashcards.a: Anycast entry at POPs, TLS termination at edge, caching, WAF (Premium), health-probe-driven origin selection, cross-region failover, ~99.99% SLA; bad probe path = mystery 502s.

flashcards.q: Pattern making App Gateway reachable ONLY via Front Door?
flashcards.a: NSG allow inbound only from AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag + validate X-Azure-FDID header equals your FD ID; or FD Premium Private Link origin removes public exposure entirely.
NON-transitive: spoke-to-spoke requires hub forwarding (NVA/gateway transit) plus symmetric UDRs; missing return-path routes cause one-way failures.

flashcards.q: How many IPs does each subnet reserve?
flashcards.a: 5 (first four + last) - capacity planning must account for it; a /29 yields only 3 usable addresses.
Stateful, priority 100-4096 custom rules lower-wins, applied subnet AND NIC (both must allow); no FQDN filtering/L7/IDPS - that's Azure Firewall territory.

flashcards.q: Private endpoint vs service endpoint essence?
flashcards.a: PE = NIC with private IP bound to ONE resource instance in YOUR subnet (traffic never public, needs privatelink DNS zones). SE = optimized route + identity claims to PaaS public endpoint, per-service not per-resource.
DNS split-brain: resolver returns public IP without privatelink forwarding; fix conditional forwarders to Azure DNS / synced records; debug with nslookup FROM the failing client vantage point.

flashcards.q: Outbound SNAT exhaustion signature and fix?
flashcards.a: Random outbound resets correlating with scale-out (ports-per-instance shrink as fleet grows, ~1024/small instances); fix with NAT Gateway (dedicated ports, static IPs, zonal) or sized LB outbound rules.

flashcards.q: ER vs S2S VPN decision factors?
flashcards.a: ER: private BGP, 1-10 Gbps class, predictable latency, FastPath bypasses gateway, weeks provisioning. VPN: IPsec over internet, near-zero idle cost, days to stand up - fine below ~Gbps sporadic needs.
Front Door access logs first: requests arriving? origins healthy? WAF blocking? Edge logs triage in minutes what backend log-diving takes hours to find.
Narrow exclusion rules scoped to specific selectors/paths, anomaly scoring analysis, never disable CRS globally; compensating controls + time-boxed documented exceptions when business insists.
